detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Detectors returned zero hits, consistent with my read that no decorative tells are present. Zero tells does not make the page specific or appealing (anti-slop principle 9; SLP-64). Nothing in the detector output changes either verdict.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical wrench glyph on a pale-green square in the thumbnail slot, the largest visual element on each card and the one place the real stock could be seen. It reads as a placeholder left on show.
findings.impact: Members who recognise tools by shape get no visual cue and must read every title; the page may read as unfinished, and the thumbnail column costs width that truncates names on phones.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail slot is for (the library's own photographs with labelled slots where missing, a per-category glyph from the one icon family, or no thumbnail); one repeated glyph does none of these jobs.

findings.title: Tool names truncated on phones, making the two drills indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut to one line with an ellipsis: both drill cards read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', losing 'two batteries' vs 'one battery'; likewise ladder, hedge trimmer and others.
findings.impact: On the primary device members may open the wrong drill; the brief's own example ('the drill with two batteries') is exactly what is cut off.

evidence.detail: first two titles both 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...'

findings.recommendation: Decide that tool names wrap rather than truncate at narrow widths and give the name the width it needs.

findings.title: Search moves below the full tool list on phones
findings.description: At 1280 and 768 the search field sits above the tool grid; at 375 'Search tools' and the filter button appear after all ten cards.
findings.impact: On phones the find page's main tool for its single job is out of sight until the member scrolls past the list; as stock grows it may effectively disappear.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same order across widths so search precedes results on phones.

findings.title: Sticky 'Reserve this tool' bar covers the calendar and the open loan list
findings.description: On the tool page the action bar sits over calendar rows at 1280 (including the selected day in day-chosen) and at 375 over the 'Pick-up day' heading and the open loan-length listbox, of which only 'One week' is visible. The bar's button ends at ~1264 px while page content ends at 1184 px.
findings.impact: Members may not see the day they just selected or the loan options they opened; on the key step this reads as unfinished. Full-page captures can misplace fixed bars at 1280, but the 375 loan-open frame shows the occlusion within the first viewport.

evidence.detail: listbox cut off by the bar
selected Monday 12 hidden under the bar

findings.recommendation: Decide the bar's relationship to content: reserve space for it, keep overlays such as the listbox above it, and align it to the content width.

findings.title: 'Added to your basket' toast overlaps the calendar weekday header
findings.description: In the added state at 1280 the dark toast sits over the We/Th column header of the calendar, covering 'We'.
findings.impact: The only feedback moment in the flow covers content and looks like a layering mistake.
findings.recommendation: Decide a toast position that never overlaps the step's controls.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar has no month label
findings.description: The calendar shows Su-Sa and dates 9-29 with no month or year caption; the status line names the month only after a day is chosen.
findings.impact: A first-time member planning a weekend job may be unsure which month the dates are in, especially near a month boundary.

evidence.detail: grid starts at Fr 9 with no month heading

findings.recommendation: Decide how the calendar names its month within the type system.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions listed latest-first, with an orphan full-width card
findings.description: The basket lists sessions from Wednesday 28 October down to Saturday 10 October; at 1024-1440 the latest session sits alone on a full-width row and the other five wrap into narrow tiles whose labels break onto three lines.
findings.impact: The nearest session, usually the one wanted, is last and least prominent; the uneven grid may look broken and slows scanning.

evidence.detail: one full-width card above five tiles, latest first

findings.recommendation: Decide the session order from the member's task and one list layout that gives each label room.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the fill behind green availability badges
findings.description: In light mode 'Available from' badges are green on a pale-green pill; in dark mode the green badges lose their fill and become loose green text while the grey (later-date) badges keep a fill.
findings.impact: Members in dark mode in the evening (the declared use scene) see two badge treatments that look like different components; available-now items look weakest.

evidence.detail: green badges without fill, grey badges with fill

findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge roles so both availability states keep one shape and the available state reads strongest.

findings.title: Filter panel uses an unthemed browser date field showing yyyy/mm/dd
findings.description: The filter panel shows a native date input with placeholder 'yyyy/mm/dd' beside a native select; the 'Category' label sits lower than 'Available from', so the fields do not share a top line.
findings.impact: The format contradicts the en-GB dates used everywhere else ('Saturday 17 October'), may confuse older members, and the misaligned pair reads as unfinished.

evidence.detail: yyyy/mm/dd placeholder; labels on different lines

findings.recommendation: Decide how members pick a date here, consistent with the pick-up calendar and en-GB formats, and align the filter fields.

findings.title: Tool details list uses two different value column positions
findings.description: Category, Deposit and Available from put values at x~224 while Chuck, Batteries, Weight and Case put values at x~180, giving one Details list two value columns.
findings.impact: Visible on every tool page at every width; works against 'careful' and makes the spec list harder to scan.
findings.recommendation: Decide one label column for the whole details list.

findings.title: Masthead identity is a small default glyph beside the name in body bold
findings.description: Every page opens with a ~16 px wrench glyph and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold body type; there is no designed mark, and the membership-card referent named in DESIGN.md is not visible anywhere as identity.
findings.impact: With the name hidden the pages could be any booking service; the neighbourly, local character has no visual carrier, so the product may feel anonymous to first-time members.
findings.recommendation: Decide what carries the library's identity on every Operate page, from its own world, without adding hero moments.

findings.title: Footer stops short, leaving an empty band of page ground below it
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280 the white footer ends well above the viewport bottom and a band of pale ground fills the rest.
findings.impact: The page looks cut off at desktop widths, including the confirmation page members see last.
findings.recommendation: Decide that the page or footer fills the viewport on short pages.

findings.title: Navigation labels break mid-phrase at 375
findings.description: At 375 each nav item wraps to two lines ('Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)', 'Opening / times'), making the masthead about 135 px tall.
findings.impact: On phones the nav takes a large share of the first viewport and the broken labels look careless.
findings.recommendation: Decide a narrow-width navigation that keeps each label on one line.

findings.title: Basket count still shows (1) after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: On the done page the masthead reads 'Basket (1)' directly beside 'Reservation confirmed'.
findings.impact: A member may think the drill is still waiting in the basket or that the reservation did not go through. Observed in one still; behaviour across navigation not assessable.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the basket holds after confirmation and make the count reflect it.

strengths: Copy is concrete, brief and in the volunteer's voice: deposit, sessions and what to bring are stated where needed (find intro, confirm hint, done 'What happens next').
One filled button per page and a conventional, well-labelled form with a linked error summary that themes correctly in dark mode (confirm errors 375-dark).
The pick-up calendar marks real session days as 'Open' (dot on phones), tying the main control to the library's actual mechanism.
keep: Keep the plain, specific volunteer copy and the Open-session calendar; any added identity must not dilute the one-filled-button, conventional Operate structure.
not_assessable: toast fade and button colour transitions (motion) from stills
whether the 1280 sticky-bar overlap is partly a full-page-capture artefact (the 375 loan-open frame shows it within the first viewport)
no-results behaviour beyond the still: search 'sewing machine' shows all ten cards with no empty message
